headline: High: shared filesystem and MCP/clipboard bridges make prompt injection, data leakage, and write conflicts plausible by default; compliance risk is lower but nontrivial.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenMetadata exposes MCP server, APIs, events, and webhooks, while Windsurf can use MCP, clipboard, and workspace files. That creates a default bridge where content from one can be ingested by the other and treated as instructions. Because Windsurf runs as the user with no self-isolation, the interaction is plausible without unusual setup.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata content is forwarded through MCP, webhooks, or copied into Windsurf workspace files/clipboard, THEN Windsurf may parse attacker-controlled text as instructions.
IF Windsurf auto-executes tool output from OpenMetadata without provenance checks, THEN prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Disable auto-execute in Windsurf.
Restrict MCP servers to trusted, allowlisted endpoints.
Strip instructions from OpenMetadata-generated text before handoff.
Use a separate workspace for any OpenMetadata exports.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction/content separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, semantics, and memory/trust data, while Windsurf reads workspace files and can use broad network egress plus model-proxy/MCP paths. A shared workspace or copied files can therefore move sensitive metadata into a third-party inference path. The pair is not proven to share a filesystem by default, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata exports are placed in a Windsurf workspace, THEN Windsurf can read and transmit them through its model proxy or MCP tools.
IF the shared data includes governance or lineage records, THEN leakage includes sensitive operational metadata.
mitigations: Keep OpenMetadata exports out of Windsurf workspaces.
Disable or restrict network egress for sessions handling sensitive metadata.
Use redacted samples instead of full catalogs.
Separate credentials and principals for the two tools.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data loss prevention.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenMetadata supports multiple instances and MCP/API/event/webhook tooling, while Windsurf can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses with shared state via local filesystem. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide without locking. The profiles show overlapping mutable surfaces, so conflict risk is high.
conditions: IF both agents target the same local repository or workspace, THEN concurrent writes can overwrite each other.
IF Windsurf modifies git state while OpenMetadata emits updates into the same files, THEN race conditions can corrupt history or content.
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use git locks or a single-writer workflow.
Review diffs before commit.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata can generate governance, lineage, and trust outputs that Windsurf may consume through files, MCP, or copied text. Windsurf has command execution and file-write authority, so if it treats those outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into code or repo changes. The pair does not prove automatic action-taking, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Windsurf uses OpenMetadata output as ground truth without verification, THEN incorrect lineage or governance facts can propagate into edits or commands.
IF OpenMetadata emits stale metadata, THEN Windsurf may act on outdated assumptions.
mitigations: Require human review before commands or commits.
Cross-check OpenMetadata outputs against source files.
Mark generated metadata as untrusted input.
Limit Windsurf to read-only mode for analysis passes.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before action execution.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance and memory/trust data, while Windsurf handles source code and open files with broad egress. The profiles do not show a specific residency or certification mismatch, so only a general compliance gap is evidenced. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is not documented beyond these profiles, low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in OpenMetadata and then opened in Windsurf, THEN retention and logging policies must be aligned.
IF the deployment requires residency controls, THEN Windsurf's network egress must be constrained to approved regions.
mitigations: Classify data before opening it in Windsurf.
Use a policy that forbids regulated data in editor workspaces.
Review retention settings for both tools.
Restrict egress to approved destinations.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls end-to-end.
